# Model and source

```{r meta, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
.ui <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Juul_2019_somapacitan"))
cat("* Citation: ", .ui$reference, "\n", sep = "")
cat("* Description: ", .ui$description, "\n", sep = "")
```

* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s40262-018-0662-5> (open access, PMC6325982)
* Electronic supplementary material (ESM; supplementary methods, Tables S1-S3
  and goodness-of-fit Figures S1-S2):
  <https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC6325982>

Somapacitan (Sogroya, Novo Nordisk) is a long-acting growth hormone (GH)
derivative that binds reversibly to albumin and is given as a once-weekly
subcutaneous injection for GH deficiency (GHD). Juul 2019 pooled three phase I
trials and built a sequential PK/PD model: somapacitan PK first, then an
insulin-like growth factor-I (IGF-I) indirect-response model driven by the
individual PK predictions. The model was used to choose the phase II doses
(0.04-0.16 mg/kg/week) for children with GHD.

The PK model (Figure 1 of the paper) has one distribution compartment with
two parallel absorption routes out of the injection depot: first-order (`Ka`)
directly into central, and zero-order (`K0/F`) through one transit compartment
(`Ktr`). Elimination is Michaelis-Menten. At low doses nearly the whole dose
leaves the depot by the slow zero-order route; at high doses the first-order
route takes a large share and the profile becomes non-linear, with the
saturable elimination adding a shoulder. IGF-I follows an indirect response
with an additive Emax stimulation of its production rate,
`d(IGF-I)/dt = Kin + Emax * C / (EC50 + C) - Kout * IGF-I`.

# Population

The analysis pooled 123 subjects from three phase I trials (Tables 1 and 2):
73 healthy adult men (NCT01514500; 24 Japanese, 49 Caucasian; 33.9 years,
74.7 kg), 26 adults with GHD (NCT01706783; 19 men and 7 women; 51.4 years,
82.5 kg) and 24 prepubertal children with GHD (NCT01973244; 15 boys and 9 girls;
8.3 years, 26.2 kg; range 6-11 years and 18.5-41.2 kg). Healthy adults received
single doses of 0.04-0.32 mg/kg or four weekly doses of 0.02-0.24 mg/kg (the
0.01 mg/kg cohort was excluded); adults with GHD received four weekly doses of
0.02-0.12 mg/kg; children with GHD received one dose of 0.02-0.16 mg/kg. Mean
baseline IGF-I was 190.7 ng/mL in healthy adults, 93.4 ng/mL in adults with GHD
and 107.9 ng/mL in children.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Juul_2019_somapacitan")()$population`.

# Random-effect variances

Tables 3 and 4 report every random effect as a CV%, and the model stores the
log-normal variance `log(1 + CV^2)`. The check below reads the variances back
from the parsed model, including the occasion-level one, so a value that the
parser altered (or a mistyped CV) fails here rather than surfacing as an odd
spread in a simulation.

```{r variance-check}
ini_df <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Juul_2019_somapacitan"))$iniDf
etas <- ini_df[!is.na(ini_df$neta1), c("name", "est", "condition")]
cv_paper <- c(
  etalka = 0.477, etalvc = 0.318, etalktr = 0.328, etalkout = 0.221,
  etalkin = 0.369, etalemax = 0.207, etaiov_lvc = 0.216
)
etas$cv_paper <- cv_paper[etas$name]
etas$expected <- log(1 + etas$cv_paper^2)
etas |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Random effect" = name, "Variance in model" = est, "Level" = condition,
    "CV (paper)" = cv_paper, "log(1 + CV^2)" = expected
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 5)
# Every eta is accounted for, and each matches its CV to the rounding of the
# 0.04560 literal.
stopifnot(
  setequal(etas$name, names(cv_paper)),
  max(abs(etas$est / etas$expected - 1)) < 1e-3
)
```

# Covariate arithmetic against the 25 kg column

Tables 3 and 4 print every parameter twice: for an 85 kg adult with GHD and for
a 25 kg child with GHD. The 25 kg column is the 85 kg value pushed through the
body-weight covariate model, so recomputing it from the packaged model checks
the transcription of every exponent and its sharing pattern.

```{r covariate-arithmetic}
mod <- readModelDb("Juul_2019_somapacitan")
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

ev_par <- data.frame(
  id = 1:2, time = 0, evid = 0, amt = 0, cmt = NA_character_, dvid = 1L,
  WT = c(85, 25), DIS_HEALTHY = 0, CHILD = c(0, 1), OCC = 1
)
# The nested IOV needs two occasion levels in the table; the typical-value
# solve ignores them.
ev_par$OCC[2] <- 2
par <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev_par, returnType = "data.frame")

tab25 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~parameter, ~column, ~kg85, ~kg25,
  "Ka (1/h)", "ka", 0.0253, 0.0468,
  "K0/F (mg/h)", "r1", 0.211, 0.0441,
  "Ktr (1/h)", "ktr", 0.0102, 0.0189,
  "V1/F (L)", "vc", 12.5, 2.61,
  "Vmax/F (mg/h)", "vmax", 0.268, 0.0560,
  "Km (ng/mL)", "km", 63.0, 63.0,
  "Kout (1/h)", "kout", 0.0252, 0.0340,
  "Kin (ng/mL/h)", "kin", 2.19, 2.19,
  "EC50 (ng/mL)", "ec50", 16.8, 16.8,
  "Emax (ng/mL/h)", "emax", 15.1, 8.60
)
tab25$model85 <- vapply(tab25$column, function(x) par[[x]][1], numeric(1))
tab25$model25 <- vapply(tab25$column, function(x) par[[x]][2], numeric(1))
tab25$pct_diff25 <- 100 * (tab25$model25 / tab25$kg25 - 1)

tab25 |>
  dplyr::select(-column) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Parameter" = parameter,
    "Table, 85 kg" = kg85,
    "Table, 25 kg" = kg25,
    "Model, 85 kg" = model85,
    "Model, 25 kg" = model25,
    "Difference at 25 kg (%)" = pct_diff25
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 4, caption = "Tables 3 and 4: typical values at 85 kg and 25 kg (GHD).")

# The printed values carry three significant figures, so 1% admits the rounding
# and nothing else.
stopifnot(
  max(abs(tab25$model85 / tab25$kg85 - 1)) < 0.01,
  max(abs(tab25$pct_diff25)) < 1
)
```

Every 25 kg value is reproduced, including the two shared exponents (K0/F, V1/F
and Vmax/F; Ka and Ktr).

# Zero-order absorption

The zero-order route removes `K0/F` mg/h from the depot only while the depot
holds drug. The model writes this as `r1 * depot / (depot + 1e-5)`, a smooth
switch that equals `r1` to within `1e-5 / depot` and closes once the depot
holds less than about 10 ng. While the depot is non-empty, the depot amount has
the closed form

`depot(t) = (D + r1/ka) * exp(-ka * t) - r1/ka`,

which reaches zero at `t* = log(1 + ka * D / r1) / ka`. The check below solves
the model for an 85 kg adult at 0.02 mg/kg (1.7 mg; the low-dose case in which
the zero-order route dominates) and compares against that solution.

```{r zero-order-check}
dose_low <- 0.02 * 85
p85 <- par[1, ]
t_star <- log(1 + p85$ka * dose_low / p85$r1) / p85$ka
t_chk <- sort(c(seq(0, floor(t_star), by = 0.5), t_star + c(0.5, 2, 24)))

ev_zo <- rxode2::et(amt = dose_low, cmt = "depot") |>
  rxode2::et(t_chk) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(
    id = 1L, cmt = ifelse(evid == 1, "depot", NA_character_), dvid = ifelse(evid == 1, NA_integer_, 1L),
    WT = 85, DIS_HEALTHY = 0, CHILD = 0, OCC = 1
  )
ev_zo <- bind_rows(ev_zo, ev_zo |> mutate(id = 2L, OCC = 2))
sim_zo <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev_zo,
  rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12,
  returnType = "data.frame"
) |>
  filter(id == 1)

closed <- (dose_low + p85$r1 / p85$ka) * exp(-p85$ka * sim_zo$time) - p85$r1 / p85$ka
before <- sim_zo$time < t_star - 1
after <- sim_zo$time > t_star
cat(sprintf(
  "Depot empties at %.2f h; %.0f%% of the dose takes the zero-order route.\n",
  t_star, 100 * p85$r1 * t_star / dose_low
))
# Same parameters on both sides: only the smoothing (1e-5 mg) and the solver
# tolerance separate them.
stopifnot(
  max(abs(sim_zo$depot[before] - closed[before])) < 1e-4,
  max(abs(sim_zo$depot[after])) < 1e-4
)
```

# Typical-value profiles: Figures 2 and 4

Figures 2 and 4 of the paper show the population predictions of somapacitan
concentration and IGF-I change from baseline for every dose group. The
simulations below use the typical subject of each trial at its mean body weight
(Table 2): 74.7 kg for healthy adults, 82.5 kg for adults with GHD and 26.2 kg
for children with GHD. Steady-state panels are the fourth weekly dose. The
IGF-I change from baseline is taken from the drug-free steady state `Kin/Kout`.

```{r typical-profiles}
panels <- tibble::tribble(
  ~panel, ~population, ~WT, ~DIS_HEALTHY, ~CHILD, ~n_dose,
  "(a) Healthy adult; single dose", "Healthy adults", 74.7, 1, 0, 1,
  "(b) Healthy adult; steady state", "Healthy adults", 74.7, 1, 0, 4,
  "(c) Subject with AGHD; single dose", "Adults with GHD", 82.5, 0, 0, 1,
  "(d) Subject with AGHD; steady state", "Adults with GHD", 82.5, 0, 0, 4,
  "(e) Children with GHD; single dose", "Children with GHD", 26.2, 0, 1, 1
)
panel_doses <- list(
  c(0.02, 0.04, 0.08, 0.16, 0.24, 0.32),
  c(0.02, 0.08, 0.16, 0.24),
  c(0.02, 0.04, 0.08, 0.12),
  c(0.02, 0.04, 0.08, 0.12),
  c(0.02, 0.04, 0.08, 0.16)
)
groups <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(panels)), function(i) {
  tidyr::crossing(panels[i, ], mgkg = panel_doses[[i]])
})) |>
  mutate(id = row_number())

make_typical <- function(g) {
  t_last <- 168 * (g$n_dose - 1)
  obs_t <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, t_last + 168, by = 1), t_last + 168)))
  dose_rows <- data.frame(
    time = 168 * seq(0, g$n_dose - 1), evid = 1, amt = g$mgkg * g$WT,
    cmt = "depot", OCC = seq_len(g$n_dose)
  )
  obs_rows <- data.frame(
    time = obs_t, evid = 0, amt = 0, cmt = NA_character_, dvid = 1L,
    OCC = pmin(floor(obs_t / 168) + 1, g$n_dose)
  )
  bind_rows(dose_rows, obs_rows) |>
    mutate(
      id = g$id, WT = g$WT, DIS_HEALTHY = g$DIS_HEALTHY, CHILD = g$CHILD,
      panel = g$panel, population = g$population, n_dose = g$n_dose,
      mgkg = g$mgkg, t_last = t_last
    ) |>
    arrange(time, desc(evid))
}
ev_typ <- bind_rows(lapply(split(groups, groups$id), make_typical))
# A single-dose subject has one occasion level; one extra record gives the
# table the second level the nested IOV needs (it doses and observes nothing).
ev_typ <- bind_rows(
  ev_typ,
  ev_typ |> filter(id == 1, evid == 0) |> slice(1) |> mutate(evid = 2, time = 1000, OCC = 2)
) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(ev_typ[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))

sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev_typ,
  keep = c("panel", "population", "mgkg", "t_last"),
  returnType = "data.frame"
) |>
  group_by(id) |>
  mutate(dIGF1 = IGF1 - first(IGF1)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  filter(time >= t_last, time <= t_last + 168) |>
  mutate(tad = time - t_last, dose = factor(sprintf("%.2f mg/kg", mgkg)))
```

```{r figure-2, fig.height = 7}
ggplot(sim_typ, aes(tad, Cc, colour = dose)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 2) +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(0.1, 1000)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose (hours)", y = "Somapacitan (ng/mL)", colour = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates the population-prediction lines of Figure 2 of Juul 2019."
  )
```

```{r figure-4, fig.height = 7}
ggplot(sim_typ, aes(tad, dIGF1, colour = dose)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 2) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1000)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose (hours)", y = "IGF-I change from baseline (ng/mL)", colour = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates the population-prediction lines of Figure 4 of Juul 2019."
  )
```

The paper's lines were read off its figures by the maintainers (single-dose
panels; peak of the line and, for Figure 2e, its value at 168 h). The figure
lines are population predictions averaged over the subjects of each dose group,
whereas the simulation uses one typical subject at the trial-mean weight, so
some difference between dose groups of one trial is expected.

```{r digitised-comparison}
digitised <- tibble::tribble(
  ~panel, ~mgkg, ~quantity, ~paper,
  "(e) Children with GHD; single dose", 0.02, "Cmax (ng/mL)", 17,
  "(e) Children with GHD; single dose", 0.04, "Cmax (ng/mL)", 47,
  "(e) Children with GHD; single dose", 0.08, "Cmax (ng/mL)", 140,
  "(e) Children with GHD; single dose", 0.16, "Cmax (ng/mL)", 500,
  "(e) Children with GHD; single dose", 0.02, "C168 (ng/mL)", 0.37,
  "(e) Children with GHD; single dose", 0.04, "C168 (ng/mL)", 0.80,
  "(e) Children with GHD; single dose", 0.08, "C168 (ng/mL)", 1.3,
  "(e) Children with GHD; single dose", 0.16, "C168 (ng/mL)", 2.3,
  "(a) Healthy adult; single dose", 0.02, "Peak dIGF-I (ng/mL)", 80,
  "(a) Healthy adult; single dose", 0.04, "Peak dIGF-I (ng/mL)", 110,
  "(a) Healthy adult; single dose", 0.08, "Peak dIGF-I (ng/mL)", 230,
  "(a) Healthy adult; single dose", 0.16, "Peak dIGF-I (ng/mL)", 365,
  "(a) Healthy adult; single dose", 0.24, "Peak dIGF-I (ng/mL)", 435,
  "(a) Healthy adult; single dose", 0.32, "Peak dIGF-I (ng/mL)", 545,
  "(c) Subject with AGHD; single dose", 0.02, "Peak dIGF-I (ng/mL)", 85,
  "(c) Subject with AGHD; single dose", 0.04, "Peak dIGF-I (ng/mL)", 105,
  "(c) Subject with AGHD; single dose", 0.08, "Peak dIGF-I (ng/mL)", 220,
  "(c) Subject with AGHD; single dose", 0.12, "Peak dIGF-I (ng/mL)", 320,
  "(e) Children with GHD; single dose", 0.02, "Peak dIGF-I (ng/mL)", 50,
  "(e) Children with GHD; single dose", 0.04, "Peak dIGF-I (ng/mL)", 105,
  "(e) Children with GHD; single dose", 0.08, "Peak dIGF-I (ng/mL)", 155,
  "(e) Children with GHD; single dose", 0.16, "Peak dIGF-I (ng/mL)", 215
)

typ_summary <- sim_typ |>
  group_by(panel, mgkg) |>
  summarise(
    `Cmax (ng/mL)` = max(Cc),
    `C168 (ng/mL)` = Cc[which.min(abs(tad - 168))],
    `Peak dIGF-I (ng/mL)` = max(dIGF1),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(panel, mgkg), names_to = "quantity", values_to = "model")

cmp_dig <- digitised |>
  left_join(typ_summary, by = c("panel", "mgkg", "quantity")) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (model / paper - 1))

cmp_dig |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Figure panel" = panel, "Dose (mg/kg)" = mgkg, "Quantity" = quantity,
    "Paper (digitised)" = paper, "Model" = model, "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Typical-value model against digitised figure lines.")

# Deterministic solve against a figure read by eye: the centre catches a
# mis-transcribed parameter or unit (which moves every row by tens of percent),
# and the envelope admits reading error and the group-mean-versus-typical
# subject difference (largest row: healthy adults 0.04 mg/kg, about +31%).
stopifnot(
  abs(median(cmp_dig$pct_diff)) < 10,
  max(abs(cmp_dig$pct_diff)) < 40
)
```

The somapacitan concentrations in children agree with the Figure 2e lines to
within 6% over the whole dose range, including the strongly non-linear rise in
Cmax (about 30-fold for an 8-fold dose increase); the one exception is the
168 h value at 0.02 mg/kg (0.43 against about 0.37 ng/mL, +17%), at the bottom
of the log axis where reading error is largest. The IGF-I
peaks agree to within about 20% except the healthy-adult 0.04 mg/kg group,
where the model is about 30% above the figure line; the neighbouring
0.02 and 0.08 mg/kg groups of the same trial agree, which points at the
composition of that six-subject cohort rather than at the parameters.

# Phase II dose simulation in children: Figure 5

Figure 5 shows mean-population predictions in children with GHD over five
weekly doses of 0.04, 0.08 and 0.16 mg/kg. Figure 5b is in IGF-I standard
deviation scores (SDS), which need the age- and sex-specific reference tables
of Bidlingmaier 2014 and are not reproduced here; the IGF-I panel below is in
ng/mL.

```{r figure-5}
ev_f5 <- lapply(seq_along(c(0.04, 0.08, 0.16)), function(i) {
  mgkg <- c(0.04, 0.08, 0.16)[i]
  obs_t <- seq(0, 5 * 168, by = 1)
  bind_rows(
    data.frame(time = 168 * 0:4, evid = 1, amt = mgkg * 26.2, cmt = "depot", OCC = 1:5),
    data.frame(time = obs_t, evid = 0, amt = 0, cmt = NA_character_, dvid = 1L, OCC = pmin(floor(obs_t / 168) + 1, 5))
  ) |>
    mutate(id = i, mgkg = mgkg, WT = 26.2, DIS_HEALTHY = 0, CHILD = 1) |>
    arrange(time, desc(evid))
}) |>
  bind_rows()
sim_f5 <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev_f5, keep = "mgkg", returnType = "data.frame") |>
  mutate(dose = factor(sprintf("%.2f mg/kg", mgkg)))

sim_f5 |>
  select(time, dose, `Somapacitan (ng/mL)` = Cc, `IGF-I (ng/mL)` = IGF1) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(time, dose)) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 168, value, colour = dose)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Time (weeks)", y = NULL, colour = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 5a of Juul 2019; Figure 5b is shown in ng/mL instead of SDS."
  )

f5 <- sim_f5 |>
  filter(time >= 4 * 168) |>
  group_by(mgkg) |>
  summarise(model = max(Cc), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(paper = c(55, 178, 575), pct_diff = 100 * (model / paper - 1))
f5 |>
  mutate(mgkg = sprintf("%.2f", mgkg)) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Dose (mg/kg)" = mgkg, "Cmax, model (ng/mL)" = model,
    "Cmax, Figure 5a (ng/mL)" = paper, "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Fifth-dose Cmax in a 26.2 kg child against Figure 5a (digitised).")
stopifnot(all(abs(f5$pct_diff) < 25))
```

The model peaks sit 9-16% under the Figure 5a curves at every dose. Figure 5
is described as the mean population prediction; averaging profiles over
subjects whose weights and random effects differ gives a higher peak than the
typical subject, and the paper's own single-dose population line for the same
trial (Figure 2e, about 500 ng/mL at 0.16 mg/kg) is reproduced within 2%.

# Population simulation and NCA

The stochastic simulation below draws 200 children with GHD on 0.16 mg/kg and
200 adults with GHD on 0.02 mg/kg, each given four weekly doses, with body
weight drawn to match Table 2. The occasion for the inter-occasion variability
is the dosing week. ESM Table 3 reports the population-simulated average
somapacitan concentration (Cavg) for exactly these two groups.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20190101)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20190101)

draw_wt <- function(n, mean, sd, lo, hi) {
  # Log-normal with the Table 2 mean and SD; weights outside the trial range
  # are redrawn, not clamped.
  sdlog <- sqrt(log(1 + (sd / mean)^2))
  meanlog <- log(mean) - sdlog^2 / 2
  out <- numeric(0)
  while (length(out) < n) {
    x <- rlnorm(n, meanlog, sdlog)
    out <- c(out, x[x >= lo & x <= hi])
  }
  out[seq_len(n)]
}

n_sub <- 200
cohorts <- bind_rows(
  tibble(
    id = seq_len(n_sub), group = "Child with GHD: 0.16 mg/kg", mgkg = 0.16,
    WT = draw_wt(n_sub, 26.2, 7.1, 18.5, 41.2), CHILD = 1
  ),
  tibble(
    id = n_sub + seq_len(n_sub), group = "Adult with GHD: 0.02 mg/kg", mgkg = 0.02,
    WT = draw_wt(n_sub, 82.5, 17.0, 54.1, 120.5), CHILD = 0
  )
) |>
  mutate(DIS_HEALTHY = 0)

obs_t <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 672, by = 2), 504 + c(0.5, 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11))))
ev_pop <- bind_rows(
  tidyr::crossing(cohorts, data.frame(time = 168 * 0:3, OCC = 1:4)) |>
    mutate(evid = 1, amt = mgkg * WT, cmt = "depot"),
  tidyr::crossing(cohorts, data.frame(time = obs_t)) |>
    mutate(evid = 0, amt = 0, cmt = NA_character_, dvid = 1L, OCC = pmin(floor(time / 168) + 1, 4))
) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(ev_pop[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))

sim_pop <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_pop, keep = c("group", "WT"), returnType = "data.frame")
stopifnot(!anyNA(sim_pop$Cc), !anyNA(sim_pop$IGF1))
```

```{r vpc, fig.height = 6}
sim_pop |>
  select(id, time, group, `Somapacitan (ng/mL)` = Cc, `IGF-I (ng/mL)` = IGF1) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(id, time, group)) |>
  group_by(time, group, name) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(value, 0.05), Q50 = median(value), Q95 = quantile(value, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 168, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_grid(name ~ group, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Time (weeks)", y = "Median and 90% prediction interval",
    caption = "Four weekly doses with inter-individual and inter-occasion variability."
  )
```

```{r pknca}
# Fourth dosing interval (steady state), re-based to time 0.
sim_nca <- sim_pop |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc), time >= 504) |>
  mutate(time = time - 504) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, group)
dose_nca <- cohorts |>
  transmute(id, time = 0, amt = mgkg * WT, group)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | group + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_nca, amt ~ time | group + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = 168, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, cav = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_tab <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result)
cav <- nca_tab |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "cav") |>
  group_by(group) |>
  summarise(
    geomean = exp(mean(log(PPORRES))),
    cv_pct = 100 * sd(PPORRES) / mean(PPORRES),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
cav
```

```{r nca-compare}
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~group, ~cav,
  "Child with GHD: 0.16 mg/kg", 153.70,
  "Adult with GHD: 0.02 mg/kg", 2.70
)
# ESM Table 3 reports geometric means, so the simulated side is aggregated the
# same way rather than by ncaComparisonTable()'s default median.
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = cav |> dplyr::transmute(group, cav = geomean),
  reference = published,
  by = "group",
  params = "cav",
  units = c(cav = "ng/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = paste(
    "Steady-state Cavg: simulated geometric mean against the population-simulated",
    "geometric mean of ESM Table 3. * differs from reference by >20%."
  )
)

# A mis-transcribed exponent, volume or Vmax moves Cavg by tens of percent
# (and the occasion variance stored as 1 + CV^2 moved the child value by
# about -30%). The bound admits cohort-to-cohort differences: the child
# geometric mean has a sampling SE of about 6% at this cohort size.
cav_ratio <- cav$geomean[match(published$group, cav$group)] / published$cav
stopifnot(all(abs(cav_ratio - 1) < 0.30))
```

ESM Table 3 reports a geometric mean Cavg of 153.7 ng/mL (CV 68.5%) for
children on 0.16 mg/kg and 2.70 ng/mL (CV 48.3%) for adults with GHD on
0.02 mg/kg. The simulated geometric means (printed above with their CVs) fall
within about 15% of both. For adults on 0.02 mg/kg, where elimination is close
to linear, the simulated CV also matches the paper's (about 47%). For children
on 0.16 mg/kg, the simulated CV is higher than 68.5%. At that dose,
elimination is close to saturation, so subjects with a low Vmax/F reach high
exposures, and a simulation from the full IIV and IOV distributions has a
heavier upper tail than one from the 24 children's empirical Bayes estimates,
which shrink towards the typical value. The paper does not report other NCA
quantities for the model, so Cavg is the only published NCA reference.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **No model code.** The article states that full model scripts for the final
  PK and PK/PD models are in the ESM; the ESM published with the article
  (one Word document) contains supplementary methods, Tables S1-S3 and the
  goodness-of-fit figures but no model code. The structure is taken from
  Figure 1 and the Results text.
- **Zero-order route stops when the depot is empty.** Figure 1 draws a
  zero-order `K0/F` transfer from the absorption compartment, which can only
  run while that compartment holds drug. The paper does not say how the stop
  was coded; the model uses a smooth switch `depot / (depot + 1e-5 mg)`, which
  the closed-form check above shows is exact to within 1e-4 mg.
- **Residual error scale for somapacitan.** Table 3 prints 'Experimental error
  adults 0.377' and 'children 0.425' without saying whether these are
  variances or standard deviations of the log-scale error. Table 4 prints the
  IGF-I errors as standard deviations (ng/mL and %), so the somapacitan values
  are read as standard deviations too.
- **Variance conversion.** IIV and IOV are reported as CV%; they are converted
  with `omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)`.
- **Shared random effects.** One IIV and one IOV act on K0/F, V1/F and Vmax/F
  together (Table 3, footnote a), equivalent to a random effect on 1/F; they
  carry the `etalvc` / `etaiov_lvc` names.
- **Occasion-level variance written as a number.** The IOV variance is
  written as the literal 0.04560 (`log(1 + 0.216^2)`) because the `ini()`
  parser drops an enclosing `log()` from a variance that carries a `| OCC`
  condition; the random-effect check above confirms every stored variance.
- **Occasion.** The paper does not define the occasion of the IOV. The model
  takes an `OCC` column and the simulations above use one occasion per weekly
  dose.
- **IGF-I baseline.** The IGF-I state starts at the drug-free steady state
  `Kin/Kout` (with the subject's random effects), consistent with Figure 1;
  the paper does not describe a separately estimated baseline.
- **Emax relationship.** The abstract calls the IGF-I relationship
  'sigmoidal', but Figure 1 and Table 4 give a hyperbolic Emax with no Hill
  coefficient; the hyperbolic form is used.
- **Healthy-volunteer covariate.** 'HV' in Table 4 is the healthy-volunteer
  indicator; it is encoded with the library's `DIS_HEALTHY` column (1 =
  healthy adult). Children with GHD and adults with GHD both take 0.
- **IGF-I SDS not reproduced.** Figures 3c-d and 5b are in IGF-I SDS, which
  requires the Bidlingmaier 2014 reference tables by age and sex; these
  panels are not reproduced.
- **Digitised values.** All figure values in the comparison tables were read
  off the published figures by the maintainers and carry reading error of a
  few percent.
- **Errata.** No correction notice for this article was found on the
  publisher page or PubMed as of 2026-11-25.
